mainTopic: Staying far from מינות and sin: רבי אליעזר's arrest, the danger of מינות, and the power of תשובה in the story of רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא
overview: This amud finishes the story of רבי אליעזר, who was arrested for מינות. He admits that he enjoyed a clever teaching of ישו הנוצרי about using אתנן זונה for a bathroom for the כהן גדול. He links his punishment to the פסוק 'Keep your way far from her', which is read as warning against מינות, the government, or a זונה. רב חסדא sets the distance at four אמות, and the גמרא notes that רבי פדת and עולא's own conduct see 'coming near' differently. The גמרא then explains פסוקים about the leech's two daughters, who are מינות and the government, and about those who go to 'her' and never return. This leads to a back-and-forth on whether people who leave מינות or sin must die, using the story of a woman who came to רב חסדא. The גמרא also tells the story of רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא, whose tearful תשובה ended in his death and a place in עולם הבא, and רבי weeps at the power of one moment of תשובה. The amud ends as רבי חנינא and רבי יונתן reach a fork between a path past עבודה זרה and a path past a בית זונות. That story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא finishes his guess about why רבי אליעזר was punished
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא completes his suggestion: perhaps רבי אליעזר heard words of מינות, enjoyed them, and was seized because of that.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Perhaps you heard a word of heresy] and it pleased you, and that is why you were seized?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of רבי עקיבא's guess, which started just before this section. He suggests that רבי אליעזר's arrest happened because he enjoyed hearing a heretical idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר was looking for a reason why Heaven let him be arrested for מינות. רבי עקיבא suggests the real cause was not some act of heresy. It may have been the small inner fault of enjoying a heretical teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: and it gave you pleasure / you enjoyed it

phrases.english: and it pleased you, and because of it you were seized?
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא is finishing his guess from just before: maybe you heard some heresy and liked it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי עקיבא's suggestion, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Enjoying a heretical idea can be enough to bring a punishment from Heaven.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר remembers the question he was asked in the market of צפורי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר agrees with רבי עקיבא and recalls meeting יעקב איש כפר סכניא, a student of ישו הנוצרי. יעקב asked him whether אתנן זונה may be used to build a bathroom for the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: עקיבא, you have reminded me. Once I was walking in the upper market of צפורי, and I met a man who was one of the students of ישו הנוצרי. His name was יעקב איש כפר סכניא. He said to me: It is written in your תורה, 'You shall not bring the payment of a prostitute.' May one use it to build a bathroom for the כהן גדול? And I said nothing to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר accepts רבי עקיבא's guess and begins telling the story. He describes a question that יעקב איש כפר סכניא asked him and admits that he gave no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids bringing אתנן זונה into the בית המקדש as an offering. יעקב asks about a non-holy use inside the מקדש, a bathroom for the כהן גדול. רבי אליעזר stays silent, which sets up the answer that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Tzippori, a city in the Galil

phrases.english: He said to him: Akiva, you have reminded me,
once I was walking
in the upper marketplace of Tzippori,
and I found a certain man
from the students of Jesus the Nazarene,
and his name was Yaakov of Kefar Sekhanya.
He said to me: It is written in your Torah:
"You shall not bring the payment of a prostitute, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 23:19

phrases.english: what is the law about making from it
a bathroom for the High Priest?
And I said nothing to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אליעזר confirms רבי עקיבא's guess by telling the story behind it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: רבי אליעזר was asked about using אתנן זונה for a bathroom for the כהן גדול and did not answer.

steps.title: The heretic's answer: what came from filth goes back to filth
steps.stepSummary: יעקב quotes a teaching of ישו הנוצרי based on a פסוק in מיכה. Money that came from a filthy source may go to a filthy use, such as a bathroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: This is what ישו הנוצרי taught me: 'For from the payment of a prostitute she gathered them, and to the payment of a prostitute they shall return.' They came from a place of filth, so let them go to a place of filth.
steps.whatsHappening: After רבי אליעזר stays silent, יעקב gives his own answer. He reads the פסוק in מיכה to mean that the money may be used for a bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is a clever wordplay: the money came from something disgusting, so it should return to something disgusting. This is the teaching רבי אליעזר enjoyed hearing, and it becomes the cause of his trouble.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: כָּךְ לִימְּדַנִי יֵשׁוּ הַנּוֹצְרִי,
phrases.english: He said to me: Thus Jesus the Nazarene taught me,
for "from the payment of a prostitute she gathered them,
phrases.notes: מיכה 1:7

phrases.english: and to the payment of a prostitute they shall return,"
from a place of filth they came,
to a place of filth they shall go.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לִי: כָּךְ לִימְּדַנִי יֵשׁוּ הַנּוֹצְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the heretic's own answer to the question רבי אליעזר left unanswered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The heretic's reading: אתנן זונה may be used for a bathroom, because what came from filth goes back to filth.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר admits he enjoyed it and names the verse he broke
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says he enjoyed the teaching, and that is why he was arrested for מינות. He broke the פסוק in משלי: 'Keep your way far from her' refers to מינות, and 'do not come near the door of her house' refers to the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: The idea pleased me, and because of this I was arrested for heresy. I transgressed what is written in the Torah: 'Keep your way far from her,' which refers to heresy, 'and do not come near the door of her house,' which refers to the ruling government.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר finishes the story. He confirms that רבי עקיבא was right and explains which פסוק he violated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fault was not believing the heresy. It was enjoying it and getting too close to it. The פסוק teaches that a person must keep a distance from מינות and also from the government.

keyTerms.meaning: keep your way far from her

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's lesson: even enjoying a heretical idea is a failure to keep the required distance from מינות.

phrases.english: And the matter pleased me,
because of this I was arrested for heresy,
and I transgressed what is written in the Torah:
phrases.notes: The פסוק is actually in משלי 5:8; here 'Torah' just means holy scripture in general.

phrases.english: "Keep your way far from her" — this is heresy,

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאַל תִּקְרַב אֶל פֶּתַח בֵּיתָהּ״ — זוֹ הָרָשׁוּת.
phrases.english: "and do not come near the door of her house" — this is the government.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִנְאַנִי הַדָּבָר, עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְפַּסְתִּי לְמִינוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story and confirms רבי עקיבא's guess from step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Enjoying words of מינות caused רבי אליעזר's arrest. The פסוק in משלי warns a person to stay far from מינות and from the government.

steps.title: A second reading of the verse: heresy and government, then a prostitute
steps.stepSummary: Another opinion reads the פסוק differently. The first half covers both מינות and the government, and the second half refers to a זונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: 'Keep your way far from her' refers to heresy and the government; 'and do not come near the door of her house' refers to a prostitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different way to divide the same פסוק. The first half now includes both dangers, and the second half is taken literally, about a זונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first reading, the government was in the second half of the פסוק. Here it moves into the first half together with מינות, which frees the second half to mean an actual זונה. This sets up the next question about how far one must keep away.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
"Keep your way far from her" — this is heresy and the government,

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאַל תִּקְרַב אֶל פֶּתַח בֵּיתָהּ״ — זוֹ זוֹנָה.
phrases.english: "and do not come near the door of her house" — this is a prostitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same פסוק quoted in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By this view, the second half of the פסוק warns a person to stay away from a זונה.

steps.title: How far must one keep away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much distance is required by 'do not come near'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much [distance is required]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question to set up the next step. It wants to know the exact distance the פסוק requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Do not come near' is vague, so the גמרא asks for a measurement. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And how much?
phrases.notes: He means: how far away must you stay to keep 'do not come near'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measurement behind 'do not come near' from step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The required distance to keep from the place being warned about.

steps.title: רב חסדא: four אמות
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the required distance is four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the measurement: keep four אמות away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vague warning 'do not come near' now has a clear measure of four אמות. This gives a practical distance to the warning.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The required distance is four אמות.

steps.title: How do the רבנן read 'from the payment of a prostitute'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the פסוק in מיכה that the heretic used. It asks what the רבנן learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they learn from this פסוק, 'from the payment of a prostitute'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to the פסוק the heretic misused. It asks for the proper rabbinic reading, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heretic read מיכה 1:7 as a halachic permission to use the money for a bathroom. The רבנן do not accept that reading, so the גמרא asks what they do learn from the words.

keyTerms.meaning: what do they learn from it?

phrases.english: And the Sages, this "from the payment of a prostitute"
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: what do they learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן הַאי מֵאֶתְנַן זוֹנָה מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of distance and returns to the פסוק from step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The רבנן's own reading of מיכה 1:7.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a prostitute who is hired ends up hiring others
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read the phrase like רב חסדא: a זונה who is hired for money will in the end pay others. The proof is a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רב חסדא, for רב חסדא said: Every prostitute who is hired will in the end be the one who hires, as it says: 'And in that you give payment, and no payment is given to you, [so you are the opposite].'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן understand the פסוק as describing what happens to a זונה over time. It is not a halachic permission for using the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From payment she gathered, and to payment they shall return' means the זונה starts by receiving payment and ends up giving it. The פסוק in יחזקאל supports this reversal. This replaces the heretic's reading with a moral description.

keyTerms.meaning: in line with רב חסדא's view

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן do not learn halacha about the money from מיכה 1:7. They read it like רב חסדא: the one who was paid ends up paying.

phrases.english: Like Rav Chisda, for Rav Chisda said:
Every prostitute who is hired,
in the end she is the one who hires,
as it says: "And in that you give payment,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 16:34

phrases.english: and payment is not given to you, [and you are the opposite]."
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording, finishing the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן read מיכה 1:7 like רב חסדא: a זונה who is hired ends up hiring others, as יחזקאל 16:34 shows.

steps.title: רבי פדת limits 'do not come near' to actual relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רב חסדא's four-אמות rule disagrees with רבי פדת, who says the תורה only forbids actual forbidden relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבי פדת, who said: the תורה forbade only the 'coming near' of actual forbidden relations, as the פסוק says, 'Any man to any close relative, do not come near to uncover nakedness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that another אמורא, רבי פדת, does not agree with רב חסדא's rule of keeping four אמות away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא treated 'do not come near' as real physical distance. רבי פדת reads the words 'to uncover nakedness' as defining the 'coming near': only actual relations are forbidden by the תורה. So for him, closeness without relations is not included in the תורה's prohibition.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with רבי פדת,
phrases.notes: 'This' means רב חסדא's rule of four אמות from step 7.

phrases.english: as רבי פדת says:
The תורה forbade only the coming near
of forbidden relations alone,
as it is said:
"Any man, to any close relative of his,
do not come near to uncover nakedness."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:6. The words 'to uncover nakedness' show which kind of 'coming near' is meant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב חסדא's four-אמות rule and shows a contrasting opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי פדת, the תורה forbids only actual forbidden relations, not mere closeness.

steps.title: עולא kisses his sisters
steps.stepSummary: עולא used to kiss his sisters when he came home from the study hall.
steps.simpleTranslation: When עולא came from the study hall, he would kiss his sisters on their hands, and some say on their chests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about עולא's behavior with his sisters. It is setting up the next step, which compares this to עולא's own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story shows עולא being physically close to relatives he may not marry. That matches the lenient approach of רבי פדת. The two versions disagree only about where he kissed them.

phrases.aramaic: עוּלָּא כִּי הֲוָה אָתֵי מִבֵּי רַב,
phrases.english: When עולא would come from the study hall,
he would kiss his sisters
on their hands,
and some say: on their chests.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא כִּי הֲוָה אָתֵי מִבֵּי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story about practice that fits רבי פדת's lenient view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולא kissed his sisters, showing he was not concerned about mere closeness with them.

steps.title: עולא's practice clashes with his own ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that עולא's behavior contradicts his own statement that even mere closeness is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: His practice contradicts his own ruling, because עולא said: mere closeness is forbidden, as the saying goes, 'Go, go, we tell the נזיר; go around, go around, do not come near the vineyard.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that עולא seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא ruled that one must stay away even from closeness, just as a נזיר is told to avoid the vineyard entirely. Yet he kissed his sisters. The גמרא states this contradiction and leaves it unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: His own words contradict his own words

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not resolve this contradiction here. Do not look for an answer in the text; it is simply pointed out.

phrases.english: And his own [practice] disagrees with his own [ruling],
as עולא says:
Mere closeness is forbidden,
because of: "Go, go, we tell the נזיר;
go around, go around, do not come near the vineyard."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets עולא's practice from step 11 against his own ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's practice of kissing his sisters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עולא himself ruled that even mere closeness is forbidden, so how could he kiss his sisters?

steps.title: What does 'give, give' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about the leech's two daughters and asks what 'give, give' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The leech has two daughters: Give, give.' What is 'give, give'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק from משלי and asks what it means. This sets up מר עוקבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic goes back to מינות and the government, which were mentioned earlier. The פסוק's picture of a greedy leech with two daughters needs explaining.

phrases.english: "The leech has two daughters: Give, give."
phrases.notes: משלי 30:15

phrases.english: What is "give, give"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new explanation of a פסוק tied to the earlier topic of מינות and the government.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'give, give' in the פסוק.

steps.title: מר עוקבא: two daughters crying from גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא explains that these are two daughters who cry from גיהנם and who, in this world, say 'bring, bring.'
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא said: it is the voice of two daughters who cry out from גיהנם, and who say in this world, 'Bring, bring.'
steps.whatsHappening: מר עוקבא answers the question: the 'two daughters' cry out in גיהנם, and in this world they keep demanding more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double word 'give, give' describes something that always demands and is never satisfied. In this world these daughters keep asking for more. In גיהנם they cry out in suffering.

phrases.english: מר עוקבא said:
[The voice of] two daughters
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: who cry out from גיהנם,
and who say in this world: "Bring, bring."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Give, give' is the cry of two daughters who demand 'bring, bring' in this world and cry out from גיהנם.

steps.title: The two daughters are מינות and the government
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the two daughters as מינות and the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who are they? מינות and the government.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the two daughters are, and answers right away: מינות and the government.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties the פסוק back to the earlier discussion of מינות and the government. Both are pictured as always demanding more: the government wants taxes and loyalty, and מינות pulls people in.

phrases.english: And who are they?
מינות and the government.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies who the daughters in מר עוקבא's explanation are.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two daughters are מינות and the government.

steps.title: Another version: גיהנם calls for the two daughters
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב חסדא quotes מר עוקבא that גיהנם itself cries out, asking for the two daughters to be brought to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: the voice of גיהנם cries out and says, 'Bring me the two daughters who cry and say in this world, Bring, bring.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of מר עוקבא's teaching, passed on by רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version the daughters themselves cry from גיהנם. In this version it is גיהנם that cries out, demanding that the daughters be brought to it. Either way, the 'daughters' are the ones who say 'bring, bring' in this world.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא,
phrases.english: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא:
The voice of גיהנם cries out and says:
Bring me the two daughters
who cry out and say in this world: "Bring, bring."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the teaching in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version גיהנם cries out 'Bring me' the two daughters. The daughters are still the ones who say 'bring, bring' in this world.

steps.title: If they never return, how could they reach life?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק saying those who go to 'her' do not return and do not reach the paths of life, and asks why the second half is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'All who go to her do not return, and do not reach the paths of life.' But since they did not return, how could they reach it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from משלי and asks why it adds 'they do not reach the paths of life.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic here is still מינות. If people never come back, it is obvious they will not reach the paths of life. So the second half of the פסוק seems to add nothing.

phrases.english: "All who go to her do not return,
phrases.notes: משלי 2:19

phrases.english: and do not reach the paths of life."
But since they did not return,
from where would they reach [it]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of מינות with a puzzle about another פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the פסוק in משלי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If they never return, it is obvious they will not reach life, so the second half seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Even if they return, they do not reach life
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the פסוק means: even if they do return, they will not reach the paths of life.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: and if they do return, they will not reach the paths of life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second half of the פסוק talks about those who do come back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two parts. Most who go to מינות never return. Even those who do return still do not reach the paths of life. So the second half adds something new.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying

steps.whatToRemember: מינות is pictured as greedy and dangerous: it is one of the two 'daughters' who always demand more. Even those who leave it do not reach the paths of life.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
And if they do return,
they will not reach the paths of life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second half of the פסוק seemed to repeat the first half.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second half refers to those who do return: even they do not reach the paths of life.

steps.title: A woman left heresy but did not die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that anyone who leaves מינות dies. It brings a woman who confessed to רב חסדא and did not die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that anyone who leaves heresy dies? But a woman came to רב חסדא and said, 'The lightest of my sins is that I had my younger son from my older son.' רב חסדא said, 'Prepare her shrouds,' yet she did not die. Since she called that her lightest sin, she must also have been involved in heresy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading of the פסוק from step 18. It brings a real story where someone left מינות and still lived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 implied that someone who comes back from מינות dies. This woman called incest her 'lightest' sin, so her worse sins must have included מינות. She confessed and did not die, which seems to break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? A way of questioning what follows from a statement.
One who separates himself from heresy, meaning he does תשובה.
The lightest of the light, the least of her sins.
Provisions for a journey. Here it means burial shrouds.

steps.confusionAlert: The woman never says she was involved in מינות. The גמרא works it out: if incest was her lightest sin, something worse must have been there, and that worse sin is מינות.

phrases.english: Is this to say that anyone who separates from heresy dies?
phrases.notes: This comes from step 18: even if they return, they won't reach 'the paths of life.'

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָהִיא דַּאֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: But what about that woman who came before Rav Chisda,
and she said to him: The lightest of the light,
she conceived her younger son from her older son,
and Rav Chisda said to her:
Prepare funeral shrouds for her,
phrases.notes: He speaks about her in the third person, meaning she should get ready, because she will soon die.

phrases.english: and she did not die.
From the fact that she said 'the lightest of the light' she did,
it follows that heresy was also in her!
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא, דְּכׇל הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִמִּינוּת מָיֵית? וְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of step 18 that one who returns from מינות dies.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that everyone who does תשובה from מינות dies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A woman whose sins included מינות confessed and did not die, so the rule cannot be true for everyone.

steps.title: She did not repent properly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the woman did not do complete תשובה, so she did not die.
steps.simpleTranslation: That woman did not truly repent, and that is why she did not die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rule. The woman lived only because her תשובה was not real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is about someone who truly comes back from מינות. Her return was not complete, so the rule never applied to her, and the story does not disprove it.

phrases.english: That was a case where she did not repent properly,
and because of that she did not die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case: the rule applies only to full תשובה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The woman did full תשובה from מינות and survived, which disproves the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her תשובה was incomplete, so the rule never applied to her.

steps.title: Another version: a woman repented from sin and died
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, the challenge is the opposite: does only מינות bring death? The woman who came to רב חסדא died, even though her sin seems to be incest.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the question was this: only someone who leaves heresy dies, but not someone who leaves other sins? But the woman came to רב חסדא, he told them, 'Prepare her shrouds,' and she died!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the challenge. Here the story ends with the woman dying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the problem is not that someone lived. The problem is that someone died after repenting from incest, a sin of עבירה, which seems to show that death is not limited to מינות.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin. Here it means forbidden relations.

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions tell the same story with opposite endings: in the first she did not die, in the second she died.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
From heresy, yes; from sin, no?
phrases.notes: He means: only returning from heresy leads to death, but returning from other sins does not?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָהִיא דַּאֲתַאי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: But what about that woman who came before Rav Chisda,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לְהוּ [רַב חִסְדָּא: זַוִּידוּ לַהּ זְוַודְתָּא],
phrases.english: and Rav Chisda said to them: Prepare shrouds for her,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and she died!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: מִמִּינוּת — אִין, מֵעֲבֵירָה — לָא? וְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the challenge in steps 19 and 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that only one who does תשובה from מינות dies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The woman repented from incest and died, so death seems to apply to עבירה too.

steps.title: She died because of heresy too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that because she called incest her lightest sin, her sins also included מינות. That is why she died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since she called it 'the lightest of the light,' she must also have been involved in heresy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second version. The woman's death came from her מינות, not just from her other sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same reasoning used as part of the challenge in step 19 now becomes the answer. Her worse sins included מינות, so her death fits the rule that leaving מינות brings death.

phrases.english: From the fact that she said 'the lightest of the light,'
it follows that heresy was also in her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the case again: her death came from מינות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She died only for repenting from incest.
steps.terutzMaskana: She also had מינות, so her death fits the rule.
steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמְרָה קַלָּה שֶׁבַּקַּלּוֹת, מִכְּלָל דְּמִינוּת נָמֵי הַוְיָא בַּהּ

steps.title: Can repenting from sin also bring death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether it is really true that one who repents from עבירה does not die. It begins to quote a ברייתא about רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from sin one does not die? But it was taught: They said about רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא that there was no prostitute in the world he did not go to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against the idea that only leaving מינות leads to death. It is setting up a long story from a ברייתא as its proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, death was tied only to מינות. The גמרא now brings the story of a man whose sin was forbidden relations, not מינות, to show that death after תשובה can happen for עבירה too.

keyTerms.meaning: A man known for terrible sins who later repented.

phrases.english: And from sin, does one not die?
But isn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דּוּרְדְּיָא,
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Elazar ben Durdaya
that he did not leave one prostitute in the world
with whom he did not have relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption, left standing after step 22, that only leaving מינות brings death.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that one who does תשובה from עבירה does not die.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא tells of a man whose sins were forbidden relations, and the story will show that his תשובה ended in death.

steps.title: The prostitute tells him he cannot repent
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells how רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא traveled far to a prostitute, and she told him he would never be accepted in תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he heard of a prostitute overseas who charged a purse of dinars. He took a purse of dinars and crossed seven rivers to reach her. During the act she passed wind and said: Just as this wind will not return to its place, so אלעזר בן דורדיא will not be accepted in תשובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story that the גמרא is using as proof. It sets up the moment that pushes רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא toward תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her words shock him. She says his sins are so great that, like wind that has left, he can never come back. This story about עבירה is building toward showing how his תשובה ends, which is the proof for the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A purse full of dinars, gold coins.

phrases.english: Once, he heard
that there was one prostitute in the cities overseas,
and she would take a purse of dinars as her fee.
He took a purse of dinars and went,
and crossed seven rivers to reach her.
During the act, she passed wind,
phrases.notes: 'הרגל דבר' literally means 'the usual matter.' It is a polite way of saying they were having relations.

phrases.english: and she said: Just as this wind
does not return to its place,
so too Elazar ben Durdaya
will not be accepted in repentance.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּעַם אַחַת שָׁמַע שֶׁיֵּשׁ זוֹנָה אַחַת בִּכְרַכֵּי הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 23 as the source for the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that תשובה from עבירה can also bring death.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא, whose sin was forbidden relations, not מינות.

steps.title: He begs all of creation to pray for him, and they all refuse
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא asks the mountains, heaven and earth, sun and moon, and stars to pray for him. Each one answers with a פסוק showing that it will not last forever and needs mercy for itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and sat between two mountains and hills and said: Mountains and hills, ask for mercy for me! They said: Before we ask for you, we need to ask for ourselves, as it says, 'For the mountains may move and the hills may shake.' He said: Heaven and earth, ask for mercy for me! They said: Before we ask for you, we need to ask for ourselves, as it says, 'For the heavens will vanish like smoke and the earth will wear out like a garment.' He said: Sun and moon, ask for mercy for me! They said: Before we ask for you, we need to ask for ourselves, as it says, 'The moon will be embarrassed and the sun ashamed.' He said: Stars and constellations, ask for mercy for me! They said: Before we ask for you, we need to ask for ourselves, as it says, 'All the host of heaven will melt away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story. After the woman told him he would never be accepted in תשובה, רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא looks for someone to pray for him, and is turned down four times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of creation answers with a פסוק from ישעיהו showing that it too will one day end. The message is that nothing in the world can do his תשובה for him. This sets up the next step, where he realizes it all depends on himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Ask for mercy on my behalf (pray for me)
We need to ask for ourselves

phrases.aramaic: הָלַךְ וְיָשַׁב בֵּין שְׁנֵי הָרִים וּגְבָעוֹת,
phrases.english: He went and sat between two mountains and hills.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: הָרִים וּגְבָעוֹת בַּקְּשׁוּ עָלַי רַחֲמִים!
phrases.english: He said: Mountains and hills, ask for mercy for me!

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: עַד שֶׁאָנוּ מְבַקְּשִׁים עָלֶיךָ
phrases.english: They said to him: Before we ask for you,
we need to ask for ourselves,
as it says: 'For the mountains may move and the hills may shake.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 54:10

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ בַּקְּשׁוּ עָלַי רַחֲמִים!
phrases.english: He said: Heaven and earth, ask for mercy for me!
They said: Before we ask for you,
we need to ask for ourselves,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי שָׁמַיִם כֶּעָשָׁן נִמְלָחוּ וְהָאָרֶץ כַּבֶּגֶד תִּבְלֶה״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'For the heavens will vanish like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 51:6

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: חַמָּה וּלְבָנָה בַּקְּשׁוּ עָלַי רַחֲמִים!
phrases.english: He said: Sun and moon, ask for mercy for me!

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: עַד שֶׁאָנוּ מְבַקְּשִׁים עָלֶיךָ,
phrases.english: They said to him: Before we ask for you,
we need to ask for ourselves,
as it says: 'The moon will be embarrassed, and the sun ashamed.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 24:23

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת בַּקְּשׁוּ עָלַי רַחֲמִים!
phrases.english: He said: Stars and constellations, ask for mercy for me!

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: עַד שֶׁאָנוּ מְבַקְּשִׁים עָלֶיךָ,
phrases.english: They said to him: Before we ask for you,
we need to ask for ourselves,
as it says: 'And all the host of heaven will melt away.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 34:4

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלַךְ וְיָשַׁב בֵּין שְׁנֵי הָרִים וּגְבָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 24 as part of the proof for the קשיא in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: The question from step 23: is it true that one who does תשובה from an עבירה does not die?
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא (continued)

steps.title: He cries until his soul leaves him, and a בת קול welcomes him to עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: Realizing it depends only on him, רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא cries with his head between his knees until he dies. A בת קול announces that he is ready for עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: The matter depends only on me. He put his head between his knees and cried loudly until his soul left him. A heavenly voice came out and said: רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא is ready for life in the World to Come!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the climax of the story. His תשובה is accepted, but he dies right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the part of the ברייתא that the גמרא needs for its challenge. He did complete תשובה from an עבירה, and still he died. That seems to go against the rule that only one who repents from מינות dies.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter depends only on me
Ready for (destined for) life in the World to Come

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: אֵין הַדָּבָר תָּלוּי אֶלָּא בִּי.
phrases.english: He said: The matter depends only on me.
He put his head between his knees
and cried loudly until his soul left him.
A heavenly voice came out and said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דּוּרְדְּיָא מְזֻומָּן לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא!
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא is ready for life in the World to Come!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: אֵין הַדָּבָר תָּלוּי אֶלָּא בִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא story begun in steps 24 and 25.
steps.raayaObject: Shows that a person who did תשובה from an עבירה died.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ending of the ברייתא about רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא

steps.title: But he sinned with an עבירה and still died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the challenge: רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא's sin was an עבירה, not מינות, and yet he died after his תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here he was involved in an עבירה, and he died!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the point of the story clearly: this is the challenge that started in step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule so far was that only one who returns from מינות dies, while one who returns from an עבירה does not. Here is a man whose sin was an עבירה, and he died. So the story seems to contradict the rule.

phrases.english: And here he was involved in an עבירה, and he died!
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording, to spell out the question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the story just told.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that one who does תשובה from an עבירה does not die (only from מינות).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא's sin was זנות, an עבירה, yet he died after his תשובה, which the rule says should not happen.

steps.title: His deep attachment to the sin made it like מינות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that since he was so deeply attached to that sin, it is treated like מינות, so his death fits the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, since he was very attached to it, it is like מינות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that this case really fits the מינות category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His sin was technically an עבירה, but he was so tied to it that it took over his life, the way מינות does. So his case gets the outcome of מינות, and the rule stays true: a regular עבירה does not bring death on returning.

keyTerms.meaning: That he was very attached to it

steps.whatToRemember: A sin that a person is extremely attached to can be treated like מינות. That is why רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא died after his תשובה, just like the woman in step 22.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying זנות itself is מינות. It is only saying that his extreme attachment made his case act like מינות.

phrases.english: There too,
since he was very attached to it,
it is like מינות.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דַּאֲבִיק בַּהּ טוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: his עבירה is treated like מינות because of his extreme attachment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His sin was a plain עבירה, so his death breaks the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: His attachment was so strong that it counts like מינות, so the rule still holds.

steps.title: רבי weeps over the power of a single moment of תשובה
steps.stepSummary: רבי cries and says that some people earn עולם הבא over many years and some in one moment. He adds that בעלי תשובה are not only accepted, they are even called 'רבי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי cried and said: Some people earn their World to Come over many years, and some earn it in one moment. And רבי said: It is not enough that בעלי תשובה are accepted; they are even called 'רבי'.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי's reaction to it. These are two lessons about the greatness of תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי is moved that one moment of real תשובה can equal a lifetime of work. His second point comes from the בת קול calling him 'רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא'. That shows that a בעל תשובה is not only forgiven but also honored.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not enough for them

steps.whatToRemember: One moment of sincere תשובה can earn עולם הבא, and a בעל תשובה is even given honor, like the title 'רבי'.

phrases.english: רבי cried and said:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who is simply called 'רבי'.

phrases.english: Some people earn their World to Come over many years,
and some earn their World to Come in one moment.
And רבי said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא דַּיָּין לְבַעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִין אוֹתָן,
phrases.english: It is not enough for בעלי תשובה that they are accepted,
they are even called 'רבי'.
phrases.notes: He learns this from the בת קול, which called him 'רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story with רבי's reaction, after the גמרא's question and answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One moment of sincere תשובה can earn עולם הבא, and בעלי תשובה are honored with the title 'רבי'.

steps.title: Two rabbis reach a fork with two dangerous paths
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא and רבי יונתן are traveling and come to two paths. One leads past the entrance of עבודה זרה, and the other leads past the entrance of a בית זונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא and רבי יונתן were walking along the road. They came to two paths. One went toward the entrance of a place of idol worship, and the other went toward the entrance of a brothel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting the scene for a new story. Two rabbis must choose between two paths, and each path passes a place of sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither path is completely safe. One passes עבודה זרה and the other passes זנות. The story is built to ask which of these two dangers a person should keep farther away from.

keyTerms.meaning: idol worship, or a place where it is practiced
a house of prostitutes, a brothel

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Yonatan
were walking along the road,
they came to a certain two paths,
one branched off toward the entrance of idol worship,
and one branched off toward the entrance of a brothel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן הֲווֹ קָאָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story of רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא, the גמרא opens a new story that again deals with staying away from sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scene: two rabbis must choose between a path past עבודה זרה and a path past a בית זונות.

steps.title: One rabbi suggests the path past the idol worship
steps.stepSummary: One of the two rabbis proposes taking the path that passes the entrance of עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One said to the other: Let us go by the entrance of the idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: One of the rabbis makes his choice and suggests the path past עבודה זרה. This sets up his reason and his friend's reply, which come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This choice is surprising, because עבודה זרה seems like the more serious sin. The proposal makes the reader wonder why the path past the idol would be safer. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: He is not suggesting going in to worship the idol. He only means walking along the road that passes its entrance.

phrases.english: One said to his fellow:
Let us go by the entrance of idol worship

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ חַד לְחַבְרֵיהּ: נֵיזִיל אַפִּיתְחָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues the scene from step 30 with the first rabbi's choice of path.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first rabbi proposes passing by the עבודה זרה rather than the בית זונות. His reason comes on the next amud.
